'''Joan Vaccaro''' is a [[physicist]] at [[Griffith University]] and a former student of [[David Pegg (physicist)|David Pegg]]. Her work in [[quantum physics]] includes quantum phase,<ref>[http://www.crcpress.com/product/isbn/9781584887607 The Quantum Phase Operator: A Review] S.M. Barnett and J.A. Vaccaro (CRC Press, 2007)</ref> nonclassical states of light, coherent laser excitation of atomic gases, cold atomic gases, stochastic Schrödinger equations, [[quantum information theory]], quantum references, [[wave–particle duality]], [[quantum thermodynamics]], and the [[Arrow of time#Particle physics (weak) arrow of time|physical nature of time]].

==Works==
She is well known for her work on quantum asymmetry, having formulated the widely used entropic measure ''A<sub>G</sub>''(ρ) of the ability of a system to act as a reference and extended [[Quantum thermodynamics#Resource theory|quantum resource theory]] beyond that of [[quantum entanglement]] at the same time.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Vaccaro |first1=J. A. |last2=Anselmi |first2=F. |last3=Wiseman |first3=H. M. |last4=Jacobs |first4=K. |date=2008-03-25 |title=Tradeoff between extractable mechanical work, accessible entanglement, and ability to act as a reference system, under arbitrary superselection rules |journal=Physical Review A |volume=77 |issue=3 |article-number=032114 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.77.032114 |arxiv=quant-ph/0501121 |bibcode=2008PhRvA..77c2114V |s2cid=26860319}}</ref> She has extended [[Landauer's principle|Landauer's erasure principle]], a key result connecting information theory and thermodynamics, to the erasure of information using diverse entropy reservoirs for which there may be a zero cost in terms of energy,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Vaccaro |first1=Joan A. |last2=Barnett |first2=Stephen M. |date=2011-06-08 |title=Information erasure without an energy cost |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences |language=en |volume=467 |issue=2130 |pages=1770–1778 |doi=10.1098/rspa.2010.0577 |issn=1364-5021 |arxiv=1004.5330 |bibcode=2011RSPSA.467.1770V |s2cid=11768197}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Barnett |first1=Stephen M. |last2=Vaccaro |first2=Joan A. |date=2013-11-13 |title=Beyond Landauer Erasure |journal=Entropy |language=en |volume=15 |issue=11 |pages=4956–4968 |doi=10.3390/e15114956 |arxiv=1310.7821 |bibcode=2013Entrp..15.4956B |s2cid=16110551 |doi-access=free}}</ref> and demonstrated the extended principle in the design of a [[Quantum heat engine|quantum dot heat engine]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wright |first1=J.S.S.T. |last2=Gould |first2=T. |last3=Carvalho |first3=A.R.R. |last4=Bedkihal |first4=S. |last5=Vaccaro |first5=J.A. |date=2018 |title=Quantum heat engine operating between thermal and spin reservoirs |journal=Physical Review A |volume=97 |issue=5 |article-number=052104 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.97.052104 |arxiv=1804.00843 |bibcode=2018PhRvA..97e2104W |s2cid=53952802}}</ref> She has established a connection between the violation of [[T-symmetry|time reversal symmetry]] (T violation) and the [[Time in physics|nature of time]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Vaccaro |first=Joan A. |date=2016-01-01 |title=Quantum asymmetry between time and space |journal=Proc. R. Soc. A |language=en |volume=472 |issue=2185 |article-number=20150670 |doi=10.1098/rspa.2015.0670 |issn=1364-5021 |pmc=4786044 |pmid=26997899 |arxiv=1502.04012 |bibcode=2016RSPSA.47250670V}}</ref>  Her work proposes T violation as the origin of [[Dynamics (mechanics)|dynamics]] which has implications for the [[arrow of time]]<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://app.secure.griffith.edu.au/news/2016/01/28/bringing-time-space-together-for-universal-symmetry/ |title=Bringing time, space together for universal symmetry |last=Jacobson |first=Michael |date=28 January 2016 |work=Newsfeed |access-date=7 May 2016 |via=www.griffith.edu.au}}</ref>

==Membership==
She is a member of the [https://www2.griffith.edu.au/centre-quantum-dynamics Centre for Quantum Dynamics] and a Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iop.org/news/member/2013/page_62117.html |title=New fellows, new members and In Memoriam in January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201033131/http://www.iop.org/news/member/2013/page_62117.html |archive-date=1 December 2017}}</ref>
